Your exploration of Panama City begins at the Miraflores Locks Visitor Center. Here, you will learn about the history and operating principles of the Panama Canal and watch ships passing through the locks.

The next stop is Biomuseo, devoted to Panama's natural world, its biodiversity and the history of how the country's landscapes formed. The museum building was designed by Frank Gehry.

You will then travel to Casco Viejo, the capital's historic center, which forms part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site. After lunch, a walking tour begins through its streets and historic squares. Along the way, you will see architecture influenced by colonial and French styles, historic churches and the district's principal landmarks.

Papallacta is located in the Ecuadorian Andes at an altitude of about 3,300 meters, on the road from Quito toward the Amazon. Along the way, the natural zones change from high-mountain landscapes to more humid forests.

The Termas de Papallacta complex has 9 hot thermal pools and 3 pools with cold water. The spring-water temperature is stated as 30–70°C, while pool temperatures range from 36 to 40°C.

The thermal water contains sulfates, sodium, calcium, chlorides and traces of magnesium. This full-day excursion combines a journey through mountain landscapes with relaxation at the thermal complex.

An optional 2-day / 1-night trip to “Paracas and the Nazca Lines” can be added. A tourist bus will take you from Lima to Paracas, where you will spend the night at a hotel on the Pacific coast.

A flight over the Nazca Lines is offered as an additional option. From the air, you can see giant figures of animals and birds, as well as geometric shapes traced on the desert surface. The price of this two-day trip is not specified in the program; the quote and its coordination with arrival from La Paz are handled separately.

You will depart Lima early in the morning for Paracas. At 8:00, a boat sets off from the port toward the Andean Candelabra of Paracas and the Ballestas Islands.

The Andean Candelabra is an enormous figure on a hillside in a bay on the Paracas Peninsula. It is almost 130 m high and about 75 m wide. The figure is visible from the sea and from the air. Its origin is unknown, and many legends surround it. One theory links the image to the “tree of life” and symbols of ancient cultures. The Candelabra lies within Paracas National Park.

The boat then continues to the Ballestas Islands, a group of 3 large islands and numerous small rocky islets in the Pacific Ocean. Penguins, sea lions, fur seals and many birds live here. There are caves and natural arches in the rocks. Landing on the islands is not permitted, so they are viewed from the sea. Dolphins sometimes approach the shores.

After a short rest, you will set off on a guided jeep excursion around Paraty.

You will enjoy the natural beauty and discover local culture in Serra da Bocaina National Park. The route passes scenic waterfalls with crystal-clear water, ideal for swimming. Short, safe and easy trails through the Atlantic Forest lead to the waterfalls.

During the excursion, you will also discover the diversity of local flora and fauna.

The program includes:

Pedra Branca Waterfall;

Poço do Tarzan Waterfall;

Tobogã Waterfall.

Next, you will discover the traditional craft of producing Paraty's famous cachaça. At a traditional distillery, you will learn how this strong spirit was made as far back as the 18th century. The visit ends with a tasting of different liqueurs and aged cachaças.

We will also visit the Ouro Branco Flour House, where you can learn about every stage of traditional cassava-flour production. The excursion ends with a pleasant afternoon coffee, featuring freshly ground coffee and classic rapadura, a traditional Brazilian sweet made from cane sugar. The tasting is optional.
